summary: Old Fig Garden sits on the flat San Joaquin Valley floor just north of central Fresno, and the most striking thing about it is the canopy — mature fig, elm, and oak trees arch over quiet residential streets so thoroughly that summer's 100°F-plus valley heat feels noticeably tempered block by block, a microclimate effect you can actually see in the deep shade cast across the neighborhood's wide lots. At 1.7 square miles, this is a compact enclave embedded within Fresno rather than a standalone city, which means daily errands often pull you outward onto Shaw or Palm avenues and into the broader Fresno retail and employment ecosystem — healthcare at Community Regional Medical Center and Saint Agnes, public-sector jobs at Fresno County and the City of Fresno, and agribusiness headquarters that anchor the valley's $7-billion-plus agricultural output. A median home value of $460,800 against a median household income near $101,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 4.6 — more accessible than coastal California but still a stretch requiring substantial down payments. Rent at $1,284 monthly, however, stays under 16% of that median gross income, an unusual affordability split suggesting ownership and renting represent very different financial realities here. With 9.6 hours of daily sunshine on average and virtually no topographic relief, the landscape trades drama for a certain lush, shaded stillness — a valley-floor pocket defined less by views than by tree cover.
